rows.name: the security tool receives secrets on stdin only and reads them back to confirm the save

assertions.native_check: Actual explicit KEY:abc read returns exactly the original quoted/backslash/dollar/single-quote secret. All six expected argv arrays independently constrain scripted responses, including write readback and the explicit read.
Actual MISSING read returns None, the typed undefined adaptation; the independent third find tuple requires account MISSING and response status 44.

Every recorded argv tuple is fed through the same unspawned security_command builder used by NativeSecurityRunner; each program is exactly /usr/bin/security and builder argv equals the independently pinned six tuples.

assertions.expression: assert.ok(calls.every(call => !call.args.join(' ').includes('back\\slash')), 'a secret must never be a process argument')
assertions.native_check: Every recorded argv is checked for absence of back\slash. The complete independently expected six arrays contain no secret, and input is present only for the interactive -i call.

The entire interactive stdin string is independently equal to the expected command with exact service/account/label, escaped quote/backslash secret and final newline; this implies the original suffix regex.
